data.description:
# The completion verifier returns a DEPENDENCY-LINK record where a `CompletionVerdict` belongs, blocking the close

## Reproduced deterministically, twice

`rebar transition b586-2fda-8a15-4260 in_progress closed`, exit 1, fail-closed (no verdict, no
signature, close refused — correct behaviour for an unusable verdict):

```
completion verification workflow did not produce a verdict:
  step 'decide@then/verify' failed: structured output failed validation:
  1 validation error for CompletionVerdict
verdict
  Field required [type=missing, input_value={'relation': 'depends_on'...: 'f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31'}, input_type=dict]
```

Two consecutive attempts, both failing at the same step. The payload differs slightly between runs but
is a TICKET-LINK record each time — attempt 1 carried `link_uuid`, attempt 2 carried
`relation: depends_on`, and both named `f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31`. So the structured-output step is returning
a dep/link object from the ticket's own graph in the slot where the verdict schema is expected. It is not
an install or credential problem: the verifier RAN and then produced the wrong shape.

## The correlated condition — hypothesis, NOT isolated

This ticket had **no children** when it last closed successfully (its `completion-verifier` signature
from that close verifies as `certified`). Immediately before these failures I re-parented its two
orphaned children under it, one of which carries `depends_on` to the other:

    b586 (story)
      +- f2f3  S1   closed, certified
      +- 6758  S2   closed, certified   —  6758 depends_on f2f3

So the ticket's assembled context now contains dependency-link records that were absent before, and the
named id in the bad payload is exactly the target of that link. That is a strong correlation and the
first thing to test — but I have NOT isolated it, and it should not be written up as the cause. A
competing explanation is simple model formatting drift on this ticket's (large) context, independent of
the links.

## Why it matters beyond one ticket

* It BLOCKS a legitimate close with no honest remedy: the only offered override is
  `--force-close`, which produces exactly the unattested closure the operator ruling prohibits and which
  epic `e369-a449-4773-48fb` has spent this whole cycle removing. So a verifier that returns the wrong
  shape forces a choice between leaving a ticket open and creating an uncertified close.
* If the trigger really is "the ticket has dependency links in context", it will recur on any parent
  whose children depend on each other — a normal decomposition shape, not an exotic one.
* The failure is fail-closed and loud, which is right. The defect is the shape, not the handling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the trigger is isolated: reproduce with and without the dependency link in context (e.g. against a
      synthetic parent whose two children do/do not carry `depends_on`) and record which one fails
- [ ] the structured-output step either coerces/validates its way to a `CompletionVerdict` or RETRIES on
      a schema mismatch, rather than surfacing the mismatch as an unclosable ticket
- [ ] a test pins that a ticket whose context contains dep/link records still yields a well-formed
      verdict — asserted against the schema, not against a sample output
- [ ] if the cause is prompt/context assembly leaking link records into the verdict slot, the assembly is
      fixed at the source rather than the schema being loosened to accept a link
- [ ] the remedy offered to a contributor on this failure is something other than `--force-close`, since
      that is the one action the close-gate policy forbids

## Reproduction

    cd /Users/joeoakhart/agent-5200-diag && export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"
    export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1
    rebar transition b586-2fda-8a15-4260 in_progress closed

The ticket is currently `in_progress` with all acceptance criteria checked, a fresh PASS plan-review
attestation, and `child_closure_findings` reporting 0 blocking / 0 uncertified — i.e. everything the
close needs except a well-formed verdict.
data.title: Completion verifier returns a dependency-link record instead of a CompletionVerdict, blocking a legitimate close
